topicName: Upgrade Strategies and Minor/Major Version Migration
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Upgrade Strategies and Minor/Major Version Migration in MySQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Upgrading MySQL databases is a critical administrative task that ensures security, performance improvements, and access to new features. However, migrating between minor and major versions requires careful planning to prevent downtime and data corruption."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Minor vs. Major Upgrades"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before executing an upgrade, it is vital to distinguish between minor and major version changes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Minor Upgrades (e.g., MySQL 8.0.30 to 8.0.35): These are drop-in replacements. They include bug fixes, security patches, and minor performance improvements. They typically do not introduce breaking changes or require data dictionary modifications."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Major Upgrades (e.g., MySQL 5.7 to 8.0): These introduce significant architectural changes, new system tables, syntax updates, and the deprecation or removal of legacy features. They require a rigorous testing and migration strategy."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Pre-Upgrade Best Practices"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always adhere to the following preparatory steps before touching a production database environment:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Perform a full logical and physical backup using tools like mysqldump or MySQL Enterprise Backup."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Review the official MySQL Release Notes and Upgrade Notes for breaking changes and deprecated features."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Run the MySQL Shell Utility (util.checkForUpgrade()) to scan for potential compatibility issues."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Using MySQL Shell for Pre-Upgrade Checks"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The MySQL Shell provides a built-in utility to analyze your existing database for upgrade blockers. Execute the following command within the MySQL Shell connected to your instance:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"JS > util.checkForUpgrade({targetVersion: '8.0.35', checkAllObjects: true})"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Review the generated report carefully. Address any schema incompatibilities, obsolete data types, or conflicting identifiers before proceeding."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Performing a Minor Version Upgrade (In-Place)"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"For minor versions, an in-place upgrade is usually sufficient and straightforward on Linux environments using the package manager."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"sudo yum update mysql-community-server"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"After updating the binaries, restart the MySQL service to complete the process:"},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"sudo systemctl restart mysqld"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Performing a Major Version Migration (Logical Upgrade)"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Major migrations, such as moving from MySQL 5.7 to 8.0, are best performed via a logical upgrade (Dump and Reload) to ensure a clean data dictionary state."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"mysqldump --all-databases --all-routines --events --triggers --secure-auth -u root -p > full_backup.sql"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the new version of MySQL is installed on the destination server, import the dump file:"},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"mysql -u root -p < full_backup.sql"},{"order":26,"type":"subheading","text":"Post-Upgrade Tasks"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"Immediately after a major upgrade, you must run the mysql_upgrade utility (for versions prior to 8.0.16) or execute the equivalent manual checks. For MySQL 8.0, restart the server and run mysql_upgrade if necessary, or let the server automatically update system tables."},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"mysql_upgrade -u root -p"},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"Finally, run ANALYZE TABLE on your critical tables to update optimizer statistics, and monitor your error logs for any unexpected deprecation warnings."}]
